Not published.** Jack Sandor · Council · challenger. Scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom of the page and is Joa's to apply or reject. Evidence base is the authorized 2026 campaign site: home, ten-part platform (housing, homelessness, crime and public safety, transportation, climate, local business, arts, good governance, reconciliation, miscellaneous), and the dated campaign blogs. Challenger: no 2022–26 City term, so no Record lines and no incumbent haircut. 2026 plan taken at face value. ## Card
Field Value
Name Jack Sandor
Office Council
Kind chal (no 2022–26 City term — 2026 plan taken at face value, no record haircut)
Platform URL (2026) [https://www.jacksandor.ca/platform](https://www.jacksandor.ca/platform)

### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **—** No cap, no formula, no year-path. Densification is offered as a way to "keep property tax increases down"; that is a land-use theory, not a tax rule. Cell 13 is a dash. — —
Downtown order M26 / M27 **—** No Public Order Team and no bylaw-hours position. CRCL funding is scored once, on row 7, as civilian crisis response, not as M26/M27. — —
Housing M6 **said** Missing-middle and family-suitable housing, plus "housing of all kinds, especially deeply affordable." No unit target and no 25/20/15 composition shares. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing](https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing) retrieved 2026-09-02
Household bill M66d **—** Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number are not mentioned. — —
Written program — **yes** An authorized campaign site with a complete ten-part platform (housing, homelessness, safety, transportation, climate, business, arts, governance, reconciliation, miscellaneous) plus dated blogs. Written and current. No costed budget, no tax formula, no unit target, no implementation calendar. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/platform](https://www.jacksandor.ca/platform) retrieved 2026-09-02
## The 12 topics Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date**. A dash is unknown, not a fail. No topic gets its own letter. Area columns stay blank. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Close 2.0** "The city should make it easier to build Missing Middle housing, so that nobody is forced to choose between living in Victoria and raising a family." · Commits × Comparable: missing middle and family-suitable forms named (townhomes, rowhomes, houseplexes, more bedrooms), plus the plank headline "housing of all kinds, especially deeply affordable." Not 25/20/15, no unit target. Same-plank mansion tax to fund non-market is this cluster, not a second mark. Feb 2026 REIT post on vacancy-as-mechanism is diagnosis, not a 5% target, and is not scored here. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing](https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing) retrieved 2026-09-02
2 M6b land bank + co-ops **Close 2.0** "The city should pilot a financing program for these co-op projects, and once successful, the provincial government can adopt it province-wide." · Commits × Comparable: co-op financing, not a land-bank acquisition fund or 99-year leasehold. Described as near revenue-neutral. Non-market fee exemption is scored on row 5, not here. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing](https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing) retrieved 2026-09-02
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening **Close 2.0** "The city should introduce guaranteed response timelines, where the answer is an automatic yes if no response is received from the city by the deadline." · Commits × Comparable: a permit-time instrument with deemed approval, starting at "say, 8 months" and ratcheting down. No published 90-day-class benchmark and no AI pre-screening. Pattern-book stream is scored on row 4. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing](https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing) retrieved 2026-09-02
4 M7b pattern-book housing **Close 2.0** "Building townhomes should not require a bespoke application process every single time." · Commits × Comparable: expand the provincial catalogue of pre-approved designs. Same job as a city pattern book, not the city's own duplex/triplex/townhome/laneway book. One cluster with the catalogue heading on the same plank. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing](https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing) retrieved 2026-09-02
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty **Close 2.0** "The city should commit to not further raising taxes on new homebuyers and renters." · Commits × Comparable: freeze on new housing taxes/charges/fees, plus same-plank permanent exemption of non-market housing from all taxes, charges and fees, plus the 29 Jan 2026 blog's course "to a world without" DCCs. No 5% vacancy target and no suite amnesty. Backyard-suite "cumbersome" sits inside the missing-middle paragraph already used on row 1. One cluster. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing](https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team — No unified command, co-location, or downtown operations desk. CRCL is scored on row 7. The street-interaction audit is noted under working notes and is not a Public Order Team. — —
7 M26b civilian crisis response **Aligned 3.0** "Increase funding for CRCL and other non-police repsonse programs, to better respond to community members in crisis." · Commits × Same instrument: CRCL named. Context, same plank: "not being overly reliant on police for everything" so police can "do actual police work." No dispatch criteria, no funding figure, no published diversion number. Typo "repsonse" is in the source. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/crime-and-public-safety](https://www.jacksandor.ca/crime-and-public-safety) retrieved 2026-09-02
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — No bylaw-enforcement hours position. Full ten-part platform checked. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement — No position on targeting chronic disorder drivers with data. Construction-bylaw fine increases are noise/traffic on job sites, not this measure. — —
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws — No daytime-sheltering bylaw position. "Some level of enforcement is necessary" on the homelessness plank is a Mention of enforcement, so a dash. — —
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) — Drug-use buffers, CDSA enforcement around child-focused spaces, and seizure are not mentioned. — —
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting — No named-space reclaim, no encampment-removal protocol, no night lighting. The proposed independent audit of Police and Bylaw interactions with people living on the street (belongings, retrieval) is a process review, not M34–M37's reclaim programme. Mention, so a dash. Recorded in working notes. — —
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) — "By encouraging more effecient use of our limited land, we can keep property tax increases down without cutting funding to the essential services" is a predicted result of densification, not a cap, formula, year-path or override rule. Mentions of tax restraint without a tax instrument dash every column. Same sentence is not M69 (City holdings). Typo "effecient" is in the source. — —
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule — No over-collection refund, no debt rule, no supermajority override. — —
15 M66d the Household Bill — The combined household number, water, sewer and stormwater do not appear. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger **Partial 1.0** "We need to change our funding model to one which allows cities and regions to fund transit if they want to, and we need to advocate to the province for a significant increase in transit funding, both for day-to-day operations, as well as necessary capital expenditures like a new transit yard." · Commits × Neither: a provincial-funding ask, no published ledger, no refusal threshold. Bus lanes and signal priority on the same transportation plank are scored on row 28, not here. Commercial-vacancy-tax advocacy is scored on row 18. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/transportation](https://www.jacksandor.ca/transportation) retrieved 2026-09-02
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — CRD appears only as the channel for rail advocacy, already inside the transportation cluster on row 28. Regional water rates and the filtration plant do not appear. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Close 2.0** "We must advocate to the province for a commercial vacancy tax, to tip the scales in favor of actually using valuable downtown space instead of hoarding it for speculative purposes." · Commits × Comparable: downtown vacancy instrument, provincial ask rather than a City vacancy target, Strategic Economic Plan, or "one mandate not a new office." Same-plank home-based businesses, stacked industrial units, and hotels are this cluster, not second marks. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/local-business-and-the-economy](https://www.jacksandor.ca/local-business-and-the-economy) retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — No 15-minute grace, no first-hour (gated Year 2), no capital-approval threshold, no permit-fee schedule. The platform-summary bullet on accessible downtown parking is accessibility, scored as context on row 29, not as M75. Bike Valets are cycling infrastructure, context on row 27. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. **Close 2.0** "This could include establishing regular meetings between Council and local Nation leadership, involving Indigenous representatives earlier in relevant planning processes, and seeking Indigenous input on major projects and policies." · Commits to "more consistent opportunities" for Nations in City decisions × Comparable: a standing-meeting table, cultural-awareness training for councillors and staff, and enabling Songhees and Xʷsepsəm (Esquimalt) development of the Matullia lands in Rock Bay. Not the full Foundation package (procurement target, place-names programme, urban Indigenous liaison). "Could include" is noted; ambiguity resolves up from Partial+. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/reconciliation](https://www.jacksandor.ca/reconciliation) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) **Close 2.0** "The city should strengthen the tenant protection bylaw, to encourage development of owner-occupied housing." · Commits × Comparable: expand the existing tenant-protection bylaw. Not STR licensing, not indoor heat. Same-cluster homelessness plank: change zoning so redevelopment is not concentrated where displacement is highest. One cluster. M9c struck — not scored. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing](https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing) retrieved 2026-09-02
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — No rules-based digital allocation design. Supportive-housing throughput is scored on row 23. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput **Close 2.0** "Building on work by councillor Loughton and colleagues in Vancouver, we should hire a staff member whose job will be to ensure that people are helped along to the next stage as soon as they're ready, freeing up badly needed space for others." · Commits × Comparable: a STEP-like throughput instrument on the supportive-housing continuum. No Housing First name, no 50% unsheltered target, no quarterly count. Same-cluster rent-bank funding to "keep people housed" is prevention, not a second mark. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/homelessness](https://www.jacksandor.ca/homelessness) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 6 · Families
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
24 M12/M13b/M13c childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is \$0 → M13d) **Close 2.0** "We should build on their success and build our own municipally-run clinic." · Commits × Comparable: Colwood/Langford municipal-clinic model to attract family doctors. Childcare spaces and the 18–25 cohort are not named. School food is \$0 and lives on M13d, next row. School-gym arts use is scored on row 39, not here. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/miscellaneous](https://www.jacksandor.ca/miscellaneous) retrieved 2026-09-02
25 M13d standing School District 61 agreement — No standing SD61 agreement and no school-food instrument. Using school gyms for arts events is scored once, on row 39. — —
### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm — Graffiti, pests, sanitation hours and public art do not appear. Washrooms are scored on row 29. Construction cardboard recycling is climate-side context on row 48. — —
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) **Close 2.0** "Increase traffic enforcement, to keep our roads safe for everyone." · Commits × Comparable: traffic-enforcement as a road-safety instrument, plus same-plank "legalizing actually visible road paint" against "traffic violence." Not a Vision Zero audit, not M38 calming design. M39 30 km/h is struck — not scored. Bike Valets and extended hours are this mobility cluster, not a second mark. Bus lanes are row 28. Pedestrian streets are row 37. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/crime-and-public-safety](https://www.jacksandor.ca/crime-and-public-safety) retrieved 2026-09-02
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls **Aligned 3.0** "Building on the success of the Douglas street bus lanes, the city should expand our bus lane network on key transit corridors." · Commits × Same instrument: City-controlled bus lanes, plus same-sentence cluster "every new traffic signal is equipped with signal priority infrastructure." Douglas Street rail preparation (City ROW ready for future rail) is this cluster, not a second mark. Provincial matching-fund advocacy is already scored on row 16. Sidewalk-gap standard is not stated. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/transportation](https://www.jacksandor.ca/transportation) retrieved 2026-09-02
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms **Aligned 3.0** "Build more public washrooms, and better maintain the ones we already have, to keep our streets clean and improve accessibility." · Commits × Same instrument: public bathrooms as walking infrastructure, city-wide, plus maintenance. No hours standard, no accessibility audit, no named location. Platform-summary accessible downtown parking is this cluster (accessibility), not M75, and is not a second mark. The full transportation plank does not repeat that parking bullet. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/miscellaneous](https://www.jacksandor.ca/miscellaneous) retrieved 2026-09-02
30 M25 fix roads first — No maintenance backlog, pothole standard or sequencing rule. Visible road paint is safety, already on row 27. — —
### 8 · Policing and published safety
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
31 M28b business security cost-spreading — Business security costs do not appear. Vacancy tax is scored on row 18. — —
32 M28d community paramedicine — CRCL is scored on row 7. Community paramedicine is not named separately. — —
33 M29/M29b VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force) **Close 2.0** "By regionalizing our police force, we can reduce costs, eliminate redundancies, and increase coordination for better results for everyone." · Commits × Comparable: a regional-policing instrument, not Esquimalt formula and not convene-and-publish. Stronger than a review; still the same goal as M29b. Feasibility FLAG in working notes: a councillor cannot bind another force — scored as published, not as Opposed. Not a defund. CRCL is row 7. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/crime-and-public-safety](https://www.jacksandor.ca/crime-and-public-safety) retrieved 2026-09-02
34 M30 smart LED lights, no surveillance — Streetlighting and the surveillance limit do not appear. — —
35 M31/M31b/M31c/M32 safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target — No safety dashboard, no crime-reduction number. The homelessness audit of Police/Bylaw street interactions is a one-file process review, not a public-safety KPI set. Voting dashboard is scored on row 42. Mention of accountability without this instrument is a dash. — —
### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues **Close 2.0** "The city should explore every possible avenue to make the creation of new arts spaces as easy and low-cost as possible, removing unnecessary barriers and fees wherever possible." · Commits × Comparable: reuse/renovate old spaces as cultural venues. Not facade grants, not a venue lease-bridge, not a heritage HIA. Arts funding is scored on row 39. One sentence, one measure. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/artsandculture](https://www.jacksandor.ca/artsandculture) retrieved 2026-09-02
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project **Close 2.0** "Explore new pedestrian streets where appropriate, to increase vibrancy and improve safety." · Commits × Comparable: pedestrianisation named, as exploration rather than a designated zone list. Context: Government Street pilot and Broad Street between Fort and Broughton as successes to extend. No signature-project shortlist, no referendum, nothing on M45c. Weaker than a "more pedestrian priority zones" delivery sentence; Close not Aligned. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/transportation](https://www.jacksandor.ca/transportation) retrieved 2026-09-02
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks — No heritage incentives, ornamental lighting or parks programme. Boulevard gardens are scored as context on row 49. Alcohol-in-parks pilot is miscellaneous, not this measure. — —
39 M50/M50b/M51/M52 culture, sport, and the arts funding floor **Close 2.0** "Increase arts and culture funding, to keep our arts scene healthy and vibrant." · Commits × Comparable: an arts-funding increase, not a numbered floor, not sport. Same-cluster school-gym and underused-space activation for arts events. Venue-renovation barriers already on row 36. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/artsandculture](https://www.jacksandor.ca/artsandculture) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 10 · A smaller scored Hall
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
40 M15 managed competition — Competitive testing of City services does not appear. "Culture of experimentation" / pilots is a Mention of trying things, not managed competition. — —
41 M65 rotating zero-based reviews — "Financially responsible" on the governance plank is a Mention. No zero-based cycle, no grant test, no three-part test. Land-use efficiency as tax restraint is already dashed on row 13. — —
42 M67 quarterly performance dashboard **Partial 1.0** "Introduce a council voting dashboard, to increase transparency and make it easier to follow local politics." · Commits × Neither: a named dashboard of who voted how, following Saanich, not quarterly city-wide KPIs and not a taxpayer capital portal. Distinct from the YouTube simulstream, which is M83-adjacent and has no cell. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/goodgovernance](https://www.jacksandor.ca/goodgovernance) retrieved 2026-09-02
43 M68 overhead reduction by attrition — Headcount, attrition and administrative overhead do not appear. — —
44 M69 real-estate rationalisation — No civic land inventory, no surplus-holdings programme. "Use our land more efficiently" is private-land densification, already treated on row 13, not City real estate. — —
45 M53/M53b/M53c GIS, AI consultation imagery, LIDAR — GIS, consultation imagery and LIDAR do not appear. — —
46 M53d published municipal AI standard — Municipal use of AI does not appear. Trades background is not a source. — —
47 M54–M57 local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging — Procurement, open data, Wi-Fi and EV charging do not appear. YouTube simulstream is not open data. — —
### 11 · Climate and trees as operations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
48 M58/M58b/M64b climate, district energy, seismic **Close 2.0** "The city should do it's part to legalize these kits, and should advocate to the provincial and federal governments that they be legal for sale and installation in BC and across Canada." · Commits × Comparable: balcony / plug-in solar legalization as a municipal climate instrument. Not the 50%/2030 set, not district energy, not seismic. Same-plank cardboard recycling on construction sites, and "house more people near jobs" as emissions, are this cluster, not second marks. Housing supply itself is already scored on row 1. Typo "it's" is in the source. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/climatechange](https://www.jacksandor.ca/climatechange) retrieved 2026-09-02
49 M59–M63 trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness **Close 2.0** "Increasing flexibility to allow for more greenspace and greater tree retention would ensure that we get the housing we need while continuing to increase our tree canopy, provide more functional greenspace, and decreasing impermeable surfaces." · Commits × Comparable: a canopy/greenspace instrument without 5,000 trees / 35%. Same-cluster community and boulevard gardens. Mode share is inside transportation already scored on rows 27–28. No emergency-preparedness position. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/climatechange](https://www.jacksandor.ca/climatechange) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 12 · Neighbourhoods and integrity
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
50 M77/M78/M78b \$25M referendum threshold, 5-step process, material-change rule — No \$25M threshold, no 5-step sequence, no material-change rule. Deemed-approval timelines are scored on row 3. Experimentation/pilots are not a referendum rule. — —
51 M79/M79b Integrity Commissioner + 60-day consultation response **Close 2.0** "Councillors who own investment properties should be required to verbally disclose how many properties they own, and how much money those properties generate every month, before they make housing and land use decisions." · Commits × Comparable: a conflict-disclosure integrity instrument, also to be published on the City website. Not the Integrity Commissioner office and not a 60-day consultation-response standard. Voting dashboard is row 42, not here. [https://www.jacksandor.ca/goodgovernance](https://www.jacksandor.ca/goodgovernance) retrieved 2026-09-02
52 M79c–f lobbyist registry, FOI fee, remuneration — No lobbyist registry, no FOI-fee position, no remuneration rule. Investment-property disclosure is scored on row 51. — —
53 M80/M80b/M80c neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans — No neighbourhood-grant line, no language-access standard, no Local Area Plan programme. "Vibrant neighborhoods" in the missing-middle paragraph is already on row 1. — —
54 M82/M82b community surveys, turnout and ballot access — No survey instrument, no turnout or ballot-access programme. YouTube simulstream of council meetings is civic-access (M83), which has no cell in this 55. — —
55 M81 Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic) — Amalgamation does not appear. Biography that he once rented in Saanich is not a source. — —
## Working notes (internal, not for the cell) - **Sources read in full:** [campaign home](https://www.jacksandor.ca/) · [platform index](https://www.jacksandor.ca/platform) · [housing](https://www.jacksandor.ca/housing) · [homelessness](https://www.jacksandor.ca/homelessness) · [crime and public safety](https://www.jacksandor.ca/crime-and-public-safety) · [transportation](https://www.jacksandor.ca/transportation) · [climate](https://www.jacksandor.ca/climatechange) · [local business](https://www.jacksandor.ca/local-business-and-the-economy) · [arts](https://www.jacksandor.ca/artsandculture) · [good governance](https://www.jacksandor.ca/goodgovernance) · [reconciliation](https://www.jacksandor.ca/reconciliation) · [miscellaneous](https://www.jacksandor.ca/miscellaneous) · [Who should pay for growth?, 29 Jan 2026](https://www.jacksandor.ca/blog/who-should-pay-for-growth) · [When housing is scarce, REITs profit, 26 Feb 2026](https://www.jacksandor.ca/blog/what-reits-actually-say-about-housing-supply) · [Triage and Housing, 30 Sep](https://www.jacksandor.ca/blog/blog-post-title-one-bp4e6) · ACTW live profile (context only, not a cell). Victoria News 12 Mar 2026, Martlet, and Victoria Buzz June joint profile were read; no cell uses them where the authorized site already carries the sentence. - **Not a source, applied:** Red Seal electrician / construction resume; Homes for Living vice-president and BetterTransitYYJ board (advocacy affiliation / professional background); Livable CRD partner-grader fact (structural, not a mark); Fernwood NRG volunteering; age, renter status, fiancée, school history; third-party endorsements. Bloc membership on other files does not score. - **One sentence, one measure — the ledger.** Twenty-three sentences carry the twenty-three scored cells: (1) Missing Middle / family-suitable → row 1. (2) Co-op financing pilot → row 2. (3) Guaranteed timelines / deemed yes → row 3. (4) Expand provincial pre-approved catalogue → row 4. (5) Freeze new housing taxes/fees (+ non-market exemption cluster) → row 5. (6) CRCL funding → row 7. (7) Provincial transit-funding model → row 16. (8) Commercial vacancy tax → row 18. (9) Regular meetings with Nations / Matullia cluster → row 20. (10) Strengthen tenant-protection bylaw → row 21. (11) Supportive-housing throughput staff → row 23. (12) Municipal clinic → row 24. (13) Traffic enforcement → row 27. (14) Expand bus lanes → row 28. (15) More public washrooms → row 29. (16) Regional police force → row 33. (17) Make new arts spaces easier → row 36. (18) Explore pedestrian streets → row 37. (19) Increase arts funding → row 39. (20) Council voting dashboard → row 42. (21) Legalize balcony solar → row 48. (22) Building flexibility for tree canopy → row 49. (23) Investment-property disclosure → row 51. - **Contested allocations.** Row 42 Partial 1.0 for a voting dashboard is the weakest mark: M67 is a quarterly performance KPI portal; a vote record is a different dashboard. Drop it and the mean is 2.09, still B. Row 37 Close rather than Aligned because the verb is "explore." Row 3 Close rather than Aligned because 8-month deemed approval is not the Program's permit-time/AI pair. Row 20 Close despite "could include" — ambiguity up from Partial+. Row 33 Close, not Opposed: regionalizing is the M29b goal with a stronger instrument; it is not a defund. - **Dashed on purpose, not misses of reading.** M66 (densification as tax theory, no cap). M26/M27 (no Public Order Team, no hours). M34–M37 and M31 (street-interaction audit is a belongings-process review). M13d (school gyms live on M50). M69 (private land use, not civic inventory). M75 (no 15-minute grace; do not read accessible parking as first-hour). M83 YouTube simulstream has no cell. - **Platform-summary vs full plank.** `/platform` still lists accessible downtown parking; the full `/transportation` page replaced that highlight with bus lanes, TSP, pedestrian streets and provincial funding. Accessible parking is context on row 29 only. Full planks govern. - **Actions found that contradict a 2026 sentence:** none. No City office held 2022–26. - **Legal-feasibility FLAG, not a scoring haircut.** Regional police, provincial vacancy tax, provincial/federal solar legalization, and provincial transit-funding-model change are outside what a single councillor can deliver unilaterally. Face-test still scores the published 2026 sentences; capacity is noted, not used to mark Opposed or to invent a dash. - **Never-list:** no Lisnard / Estrosi / Knafo / Musk / Brivael / Poilievre language used as a source or analogy. - **Struck / gated, respected.** M39 30 km/h struck.
